the built sheet's props (highlightId, profileId, note, open, onOpenChange)

the provider tree the shared context composes with

scope: A shared workspace context (profileId/sessionId) in shared/providers, provided by the workspace shell; a session-wide highlights read; a note-panel container that lists a session's highlights and opens 012's note sheet for the selected one; and the panel's mount in the app document composition. Out of scope: mounting cursors or the import review (the same context enables them next); any schema change.

acceptance_criteria.text: useWorkspaceContext throws outside a provider and returns profileId/sessionId inside one; the value is defined in shared/ (no feature→feature import).
use-highlights-for-session returns every highlight across the session's artifacts, and [] when the session has no artifact.
The note panel lists the session's highlights and, on selecting one, opens NoteSheet with the caller's note.
The app document composition renders the note panel; no store hook under src/app (I4) and no feature→feature import (I3).

open_questions: 012 and 015 remain open only for hardware/live goals, but their components (NoteSheet, PeerCursors) are built and tested. 026 consumes the components; it does not depend on or close the blocked goals. Raised, not silently assumed.
D-11 (defaulted: tablet authors, desktop analyses) — the panel is an authoring affordance; its mobile placement waits for 022.
Q11 (defaulted: dock >=1280, overlay below) — the note sheet already owns its docking; the panel sits beside the document and does not change that.
The context is a small, typed seam; if a future task needs more session fields (team id, mode), it extends the value rather than adding a second context.
risks: A context defined in features/workspace could not be imported by features/notes (I3); it is defined in shared/providers instead.
A direct read of the workspace slice from features/notes would duplicate a selector fact; the context keeps one home.
highlights has no plain artifactId index, so the session-wide read filters the table; the set is small (hundreds) and this avoids a schema bump.
The note panel's list is a UI affordance that also sidesteps the text-selection conflict a clickable highlight mark would create.
